subject: [PATCH v5 05/11] kernel/api: add API specification for sys_open

reviews.author: Serge Hallyn
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that long descriptions in API documentation will likely become outdated quickly due to their length, making them less useful even if kept separate from code.

Reviewer noted that relying on auto-generated documentation updates and flagging API breakages is more reliable than manually maintaining documentation, and suggested implementing an automation step to ensure consistency.
reviews.raw_body:
OTOH these descriptions are so long that IMO they are guaranteed to go
stale anyway :)  While I'm editing a return value at the bottom of the
fn, most or all of the description is already going to be off my
terminal.

---

If every build auto-generates an update and then looks for and flags
meaningful changes (API breakages), then a) that is more reliable and b)
it doesn't matter where the docs are.

Even if there's just a three line comment above a fn, history proves
that it will not reliably stay in sync as the fn changes.  An automation
step/check is needed.

reviews.author: Sasha Levin
reviews.summary: Sasha Levin expressed concern that the API specification for sys_open should be separated from the code and placed elsewhere, such as in Documentation/, to prevent them from becoming stale and out of sync with the actual implementation.
reviews.raw_body:
My plan is to be able to have the more detailed part of these specs somewhere
else, specially as they will grow some more, but I didn't want to add this
complexity right now.

reviews.author: Serge Hallyn
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that documentation in code will inevitably become outdated and suggested moving it to a separate location where it can be automated
reviews.raw_body:
My point was just that whether the docs are inline or not, they will go
stale without that automation.  So if that's the case, then the docs do
not need to be inline.

reviews.author: Sasha Levin
reviews.summary: reviewer suggested separating API specification from code by moving it to a different location, deferring the decision to the subsystem where those specs live
reviews.raw_body:
Ah, sorry - got it.

The way I saw it working out is that the core part would be inline, but the
"speccy" part would move to a different location.  

Ultimately, this is the call of the subsystem where those specs live, and I see
different subsystems taking different approaches to this.

-- 
Thanks,
Sasha

reviews.author: David Laight
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David Laight expressed concern that the API specification for sys_open is placed in the .c file, which may lead to it becoming stale and out of sync with the code, and suggested keeping it in the header where it can be easily accessed by external users.

Reviewer David Laight expressed concerns that documenting API contracts in comments within code files is not effective, as it would require updating both the code and the comments simultaneously, leading to bloat and potential inconsistencies. He suggested instead documenting return values at the C return statement.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, 8 Oct 2026 09:20:01 -0500
"Serge E. Hallyn" <serge@hallyn.com> wrote:

...

---

The only way it can possibly stay in step is to have the compiler process
the same source text.
Then, if you add/change a function parameter you'd be pretty much forced
to add/change the comment.
Return values would have to be documented at the C return statement and
really as an extra parameter to the return.

But, IMHO, the whole thing adds too much bloat to the source files.
When you 'grep' a source file, you don't really want another match in
a big comment at the top of every function.

David

reviews.author: Serge Hallyn
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested moving API documentation to an autogenerated directory in Documentation/uapi/, which would ensure it stays up-to-date and provides warnings for changes.
reviews.raw_body:
That's why I feel all this info that Sasha has added should go into a
Documentation/uapi/ autogenerated directory.  Auto-updated on every build,
with warnings if the result has changed.

-serge

reviews.author: Sasha Levin
reviews.summary: reviewer expressed neutrality on the placement of API documentation, noting that both approaches are acceptable and willing to reformat if requested by a maintainer
reviews.raw_body:
I guess I don't mind either way: I heard both sides of this argument, and the
spec workflow is okay with either, so if the relevant maintainer asks for
changes here I'm more than happy to reformat this.

Which is, I think, the advantage here: it works just fine for the various
"kingdoms" we have in kernel-land.

-- 
Thanks,
Sasha

2026-10-08.patch_summary: This patch adds API specification for sys_open, which is a common practice to document function contracts and ensure they remain up-to-date. The discussion highlights the trade-off between placing documentation in headers or separate files, but ultimately decides to keep it in the header for better visibility.
